predecessors.name: Sasanian Empire
predecessors.text: Iberia as a Persian province ruled by a marzpan after the Sassanids abolished the Iberian monarchy on the death of Bakur III in 580

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Iberia (Caucasian Iberia)
predecessors.text: the Kingdom of Iberia (Cliopatria's Caucasian Iberia row ends in 533; the page has the monarchy last under Bakur III, d.

successors.name: Kingdom of the Iberians
successors.text: Klarjeti, the patrimonial duchy where the last Iberian prince Ashot I established himself in 813

successors.name: Emirate of Tbilisi
successors.text: Tbilisi and the neighbouring lands taken by Marwan II in 735/736

successors.name: Kingdom of Kakheti-Hereti
successors.text: Kakheti, named on the page as the Chosroid retreat

ledger.x: 588: Maurice sends Guaram I to rule Iberia.

627: Heraclius's intervention replaces the Guaramids with the pro-Byzantine Chosroids (Adarnase I, 627-637/642): 'Heraclius attacked Tbilisi in 626', Stephen I died, and Heraclius 'reinstated a member of the more pro-Byzantine Chosroid house'.
736: the princely seat leaves Tbilisi for Uplistsikhe (infobox: Tbilisi c.
736: an Arab emir is installed at Tbilisi.
736: the fighting over Tbilisi ends with the emirate.

c. 748: the Nersianids replace the Guaramids for a generation. 'The Guaramids were briefly succeeded by the Nersianids between c. 748 and 779/80'; the Guaramids 'had vanished once and for all by 786'. Same state, same colour.
813: the princely seat moves to Artanuji (infobox: Artanuji c.
813: the last Iberian prince leaves Kartli for Klarjeti.

wars.name: Arab-Khazar wars
wars.outcome: Al-Jarrah took Tiflis in 724 and brought Caucasian Iberia under Muslim suzerainty; Marwan ibn Muhammad pushed into Iberia in c.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary or an area; Kartli is the core, the Tbilisi enclave from 736 is a radius reading.
